us14_wages.topic: Wages vs prices over time, Israel and US (CPI, average wages, household income, inflation history)

claims.text: Israel's annual inflation peaked at 445% in 1984 (prices rose about 5.5 times in a year); the 1985 stabilisation plan froze the exchange rate, prices and wages and drew on a US grant; three zeros were removed (1 new shekel = 1,000 old shekels); inflation stayed around 20% until the mid-1990s; a long-term 1–3% target was set in the early 2000s

Bank of Israel (Nov 2014): gross real wage per employee job rose 0.8% a year from 1996, fell 0.2% a year from 2001 and rose 0.7% a year from 2003; output per employee grew about 1.0% a year from 1990; wage-to-productivity ratio stable since 2003; Israel's wage growth similar to the average of 19 OECD members over 20 years; 2012 hourly wage about 74.7% of the OECD average (PPP)
Taub Center (reported by Globes, May 2016): no rise in Israeli real wages for at least fifteen years to end-2014; CPI rose 32% over 2000–2014 and nominal wages rose in line

OECD average annual wages, USD PPP 2024 prices: Israel 49,340 (2000), 46,050 (2010), 51,659 (2020), 54,736 (2024); United States 64,928 (2000), 71,439 (2010), 82,783 (2020), 82,933 (2024). Israel +10.9% 2000–2024, US +27.7%; Israel's average fell from 76% to 66% of the US level

Israel's average monthly wage per employee post was NIS 14,672 in March 2025 and NIS 13,907 in April 2025 (initial, CBS); April 2025 nominal +3.6% year on year, equal to inflation, so about 0% real; March +4.9% nominal, +1.5% real; about 4.1 million employee posts; tech average NIS 36,731

US real median household income was $87,460 in 2025, up 2.6% from $85,210 in 2024, the highest since the series began in 1967; post-tax median $76,060; from 1967 to 2025 pre-tax income rose about 56% at the 10th and 50th percentiles and about 121% at the 90th; 90/10 ratio 9.23 (1967) to 13.06 (2025)
Israel CPI: annual inflation 1.6% in June 2026, a five-year low, within the Bank of Israel's 1–3% target
Israel CPI: annual inflation 1.6% in September 2026 (1.5% in August); housing component 3.8%

US CPI-U rose 3.7% in the 12 months to September 2026 (0.6% in the month, seasonally adjusted); energy +20.4%, gasoline +34.2%, food +2.5%, food at home +1.8%, shelter +3.2%, core +2.6%, medical care services +2.5%, used cars -1.5%
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Globes: fuel prices fell 3.1% in June 2026; home prices in April-May 2026 were 2% lower than a year earlier

us14_housing.topic: Housing price- and rent-to-income over time, Israel and US

claims.text: Buying an average Israeli home took 155 average monthly salaries (12.9 years) in 2022 (average home NIS 1.87m; average monthly salary NIS 12,100), by CBS data; the Ministry of Construction and Housing's estimate for 2014 was 146 salaries; Jerusalem 26.9 years, Tel Aviv 22.2, Beersheba 10

In 2010 an average-priced Israeli apartment cost 129 average monthly salaries (survey published by the Housing and Construction Minister); rents rose 34% on average 2005–2011 and 49% in Gush Dan (CBS); the tent protest began 14 July 2011 when Daphni Leef pitched a tent in Tel Aviv; the 3 September 2011 march drew an estimated 460,000 nationwide

Israel's dwelling price index (CBS) rose about 225.6% nominal and 135.8% real from 2008 to 2025 (Global Property Guide compilation); year-on-year real changes included +15.4% (2009), +10.0% (2021), -3.8% (2023), -3.6% (2025)

Israeli home prices rose 0.5% year on year by the autumn 2025 reading, after a 7.8% peak earlier in 2025; Q3 2025 average prices: Tel Aviv NIS 3.025m, Jerusalem NIS 2.899m, South NIS 1.567m; Bank of Israel rate cut to 4.25%

The Alrov Institute's Housing Affordability Index measures the ability to buy a four-room flat in 12 cities each quarter from Tax Authority transactions, CBS after-tax household income and Bank of Israel mortgage rates

US national single-family price-to-income ratio (JCHS): 3.2 in the 1990s, 4.1 in 2019, 5.0 in 2024, nearly matching record highs; median prices rose 48% 2019–2024 vs median income 22%; San Jose over 12
JCHS 2026: 22.7 million US renter households (49%) were cost-burdened in 2024, a record; units renting under $1,000 fell from 8.3m (2014) to 5.8m (2024)

JCHS 2026: about 24% of US owner households (20.7m) were cost-burdened in 2024, up 4m since 2019; in March 2026, 23% of listed homes were affordable to households earning $75,000 or less, down from 49% in March 2019
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Globes also gives Bnei Brak 25.4 years and Haifa 10.1 years of the average wage to buy an apartment (2022, CBS)
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): JCHS 2024 metro ratios include Los Angeles 10.8, San Francisco 10.5, Honolulu 10.3, Miami 8.0, New York 7.3, Boston 6.6, Akron 2.9, McAllen 2.9, Toledo 2.8
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): years with negative real house-price change in the GPG table: 2018 (-1.55%), 2023 (-3.84%), 2025 (-3.57%)
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Q3 2025 average price in the North NIS 1.564m; the Bank of Israel's cut to 4.25% was its first 'in almost two years'

us14_basket.topic: The basket: price levels, food, phones, childcare, college, health, debt, household budgets

claims.text: OECD Economic Survey of Israel 2025 has a chapter on the high cost of living, recommending removal of trade barriers: cutting red tape, easing border processes and lowering tariffs; Israel ranked fourth-highest in OECD comparable price levels; OECD said the high cost of living 'continues to reduce welfare and spur social tensions'

OECD Ecoscope (Frohm, Apr 2025) attributes Israel's high prices to distance from trading partners, tense relations with neighbours, difficult border procedures, complex regulatory standards and agricultural tariffs; recommends lowering tariffs on vegetables, fruit and dairy; recalls the 2011 cottage-cheese boycott, the 2014 'Milky' protest and 2022 protests over pasta prices

OECD data reported in July 2024: Israel's food and beverage price level 52% above the developed-country average (second to South Korea); dairy and eggs +64%, bread and grains +49%, meat +64%, cars +52% (highest in OECD); telecom 30% below average, the only category below; in 2022 Israel had the OECD's highest overall price level, 38% above the member average

Communications Minister Moshe Kahlon told the cabinet (Dec 2012) the mobile reform saved the public NIS 5.7bn in two years: average cost per minute fell from NIS 0.42 to 0.10; average monthly spending per user fell from NIS 145 (2010) to NIS 93 (-36%); device import reform cut device prices 60% (minister's own figures)

Bahar (Brookings, 2016): a 2012 telecom competition reform cut Israelis' mobile bills by over 70% on average; Israeli manufacturing (incl. food producers) about 70% more concentrated than the OECD average, services about 100% more; low import penetration

Following the Trajtenberg Committee, the Knesset extended the Compulsory Education Law to all 3–4-year-olds from the 2012–13 school year; average parental payment for 3–4-year-olds fell 11.5% while spending per child aged 2–5 fell only 3% (Taub)
The Knesset Finance Committee approved NIS 1.3bn extra for the Education Ministry to make preschool free for most 3–4-year-olds from September 2012; ministry plan: 2,500 new classes in four years
Hebrew University annual bachelor's tuition for Israeli citizens in 2025/26: NIS 12,017, set by the Council for Higher Education and linked to the CPI

College Board 2025–26: average published tuition and fees $11,950 at public four-year in-state, $45,000 at private nonprofit four-year, $4,150 at public two-year; net tuition after grants at public four-year in-state about $2,300, down from a $4,450 peak in 2012–13 (2025 dollars)
College Board data (NCAN, Nov 2025): public four-year in-state published tuition about $5,940 in 1995–96 in 2025 dollars, peaking near $12,810 around 2015–16, $11,950 in 2025–26

Taub 2014: private share of Israel's national health expenditure 39.9% in 2012 (public 60.1% vs OECD 76.1%, US 47.8%); out-of-pocket health spending 2.05% of GDP in Israel vs 1.80% in the US and 1.47% OECD average (2011); real private health spending per person +69.5% 1995–2011 vs public +20.8%; about 80% hold supplementary insurance

KFF 2025: average annual premium for employer family coverage $26,993 (single $9,325); workers contribute $6,850 (26%); family premiums +6% in 2025 and +26% over five years vs wages +28.6% and inflation +23.5%; average single deductible $1,886

NY Fed Q2 2026: US household debt $18.771tn; mortgages $13.117tn, credit cards $1.263tn, auto $1.713tn, student loans $1.651tn; 4.7% of debt in some stage of delinquency; credit-card 90+ day transition 6.97%
Bank of Israel: Israeli household debt about NIS 890bn at end Q3 2025 (from NIS 846bn end-2024), of which housing about NIS 644bn (+8% a year) and non-housing NIS 246bn
Globes (Sept 2025, citing Helgi Library and TheGlobalEconomy): household debt 42.3% of GDP in Israel vs 69.2% in the US (2024); Israel's mortgage debt 30% of GDP

BLS CE 2024: average consumer unit spent $78,535 on income before taxes of $104,207; housing $26,266 (33.4%), transportation $13,318 (17.0%), food $10,169 (12.9%), personal insurance and pensions $9,797 (12.5%), healthcare $6,197 (7.9%), education $1,569 (2.0%)

BLS CE 1984: average consumer unit income before taxes $23,464, expenditures $21,975; housing $6,674, transportation $4,304, food $3,290, personal insurance and pensions $1,897, health care $1,049, education $303; 2.6 persons

CBS Household Expenditure Survey 2010: average Israeli household consumption expenditure NIS 13,496 a month; 35% on housing and home maintenance; housing and food half of spending for the bottom fifth, a third for the top fifth
Israel's 2023 CPI basket weights: housing 26% (24.7% two years earlier), food 18.3%, transport and telecoms 17.5%

us14_protests.topic: 2011 cottage-cheese boycott, tent protests and the Trajtenberg Committee

claims.text: Israel lifted state price supervision of dairy products in 2006; by June 2011 cottage cheese had risen nearly 40% in three years to just over $2 for a 9-ounce tub; butter +39.1%, cream +69%; a Facebook boycott page started by Yitzhak (Itzik) Alrov drew 90,000 members within a week; Finance Minister Steinitz pledged to 'break the monopoly' in dairy; Tnuva main producer

On 30 June 2011 Tnuva, Strauss and Tara cut the price of a 250g cottage cheese container by about 25%, to NIS 5.90 from close to NIS 8, after a two-week boycott joined by over 105,000 people on Facebook

Al Jazeera timeline: tent camp on Rothschild Boulevard against high rents dated 17 July 2011; about 300,000 demonstrated on 6 August; an estimated 400,000 nationwide on 3 September; on 26 July Netanyahu announced 50,000 homes and student transport subsidies; a committee he appointed first met 9 August
Israel Hayom: on 3 September 2011 at least 300,000 marched in Tel Aviv, 40,000–60,000 in Jerusalem and at least 35,000 in Haifa, more than 400,000 nationwide

Netanyahu appointed the Trajtenberg Committee on 8 August 2011, chaired by Prof. Manuel Trajtenberg; it recommended free education from age 3, raising capital gains tax from 20% to 25%, slower growth in defence spending, competition measures in cement, ports, fuel and dairy; tax amendments approved by the Knesset 5 December 2011, competition portion December 2011, housing plan March 2012; implementation gradual

On 26 September 2011 the Trajtenberg Committee presented recommendations including 196,000 new apartments in five years with 20% affordable, free education from age three, corporate and capital gains taxes to 25%, lower prices for supervised products such as milk and eggs, 50% student transport discount; protest leader Daphni Leef said it fell short; Regev Contes said the numbers 'don't even come near what the public needs'
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): AJE timeline: 23 July 2011 tens of thousands marched in Tel Aviv; 30 July more than 100,000 in Tel Aviv with hundreds of thousands nationwide; estimate authors not named
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): JTA calls Alrov 'a 25-year-old haredi Orthodox cantor'; the Knesset Economic Affairs Committee called on the government to reinstate price controls
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Trajtenberg was chairman of the Higher Education Planning and Budgeting Committee; proposals to raise Haredi employment were left out of the employment package
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): recommendations included express buses from the periphery to central Israel; Netanyahu called the conclusions 'an important landmark in Israel's economy and society'
